Melbourne Camarilla.name: Melbourne Camarilla
Melbourne Camarilla.note: The oldest continuous praxis in Australia: Lytton, Toreador, Embraced in Bath in 1741, has ruled Melbourne since 1888 — a court of galleries, salons and ledgered boons held in the Hotel Windsor Elysium. Officers: Lumley (Tremere, seneschal in all but title, Master of the Drummond Institute chantry — and the ONLY soul who knows the Beckoning has touched the Prince three times since 2018), Sheriff Sister Fatima Salih-El (Banu Haqim, answers only to Lytton), Harpy Tania Oberon (keeper of the boon ledger), Keeper of Elysium Galileo Trevelyan. Primogen: Lumley, Dr Miriam Halpern (Toreador), Agaricus (Malkavian, of Carlton), Wid (Nosferatu, who never attends — her voice arrives through SchreckNet from the warrens beneath Flinders Street Station) and Jonathan Wright-Mellor (Ventrue). The Scourge office sits UNFILLED since 1998 — a standing insult nobody will name. Fifty-five Kindred in all, and the court suspects — correctly — that their Prince is keeping a secret worth more than praxis.

Footscray Anarchs.name: Footscray Anarchs
Footscray Anarchs.note: The west side of the Maribyrnong, held by a single Baron for over sixty years: Red Mag (Brujah, Baron of Footscray since 1962 — sired in the founding coterie's era, oldest Anarch in the country, funny, profane, and dangerous as a dropped chainsaw). Her domain is a dozen Kindred strong, feeding at Footscray Market, holding court through the back rooms of Saigon Gallery. The 1924 Cress Truce was negotiated by her own coterie-mate Luisa Calabria, and Mag honors it — technically. Open wound: the Truce's 2024 centennial revision, renegotiated without the Anarchs' full consent; Mag has been collecting signatures among the Movement to tear the revision up, and she wants the west's borders written into the next renewal in ink, not courtesy. To the south-east she eyes Fitzroy — contested ground the court never finished claiming. Every Truce renewal is her one night of leverage.

Calabria-Hecata Family.name: Calabria-Hecata Family
Calabria-Hecata Family.note: The Clan of Death's Australian branch, seated at Calabria Family Funerals in Carlton North since 1903. Matriarch Sofia Calabria-Hecata (since 2017, when her grandmother Luisa finally went into torpor) — courteous as a wake, patient as the grave, and twice as expensive. The Family runs funerals, migrant parishes and quiet debts across the continent, some fifteen Kindred in all, and its word on death is final: the dead of Melbourne pass through Carlton North, and what the Family learns from them is nobody's business. Open wound: the Truce's post-2003 renegotiations — Sofia holds that the Family signed the centennial revision under pressure and wants terms her grandmother would never have granted; the court keeps hoping Luisa wakes and overrules her, and Sofia keeps hoping nobody notices she has started visiting the torpor chamber with documents. When Luisa negotiated the original Truce at the Cress Hotel in 1924, the city got eighty years of peace. What Sofia negotiates may not.

Royal Park Sept.name: Royal Park Sept
Royal Park Sept.note: The Garou of Melbourne: some thirty Glass Walkers under Septleader Eliza Hawkins-Greene (ex-Victoria Police detective, in office since 2018 — she reads crime scenes the way Harpies read boons). Their caern sits in Royal Park; their packs hold the Dandenongs, Kinglake, Werribee and the You Yangs. They are the Cress Truce's other signatories — the treaty that ended the Razor Wars in 1924 bound Kindred AND Garou, and the sept keeps its side with police-procedural rigor: quarterly Truce Council at Melbourne Town Hall, recognition protocols, zones that are inviolate. No Kindred who hunts in sept territory comes home. Open wound: the sept is split — Hawkins-Greene's old guard honors the letter of the Truce, but the young packs, blooded since the centennial revision, call it appeasement and point at Werribee, where the Anarchs graze closer every year. If the renewal fails, the sept's restraint fails with it — and Melbourne learns what thirty wolves do to a city of five million.

simulationRules:
CONSTITUTION OF PLAY — MELBOURNE BY NIGHT (Vampire: The Masquerade, modern nights, March 2026).

THE MASQUERADE IS THE PRIME DIRECTIVE. Kindred exist only while mortals disbelieve in them. Any event that exposes vampirism to mortal witness — a drained corpse on camera, a feeding seen, footage that survives — MUST move Masquerade Integrity DOWN via impacts.worldStateOps, and any cover-up, misdirection or repair moves it back up. A night narrated with breaches and no Masquerade cost is invalid output.

THE CRESS TRUCE IS THE SECOND LAW. Since 1924, Kindred and Garou have kept the treaty negotiated by Luisa Calabria and Don Abacus at the Cress Hotel, renewed each year at the Hotel Windsor. The sept's zones — Royal Park, the Dandenongs, Kinglake, Werribee, the You Yangs — are inviolate: no Kindred feeding, no proxies, no schemes with fangs attached. Recognition protocols govern where each side may walk. Violating the Truce is casus belli that outranks every court's law: it risks thirty Glass Walkers against fifty-five Kindred in a city that cannot afford the noise. Renegotiating it, courting it, or cheating at its edges is legitimate play — breaking it openly is a catastrophe the simulation must answer with war, Masquerade collapse, or both.

NO OPEN KINDRED WARFARE. Kindred do not march armies; they scheme. Territorial gains are made by court decree, negotiated cession, betrayal, and pressure — not by set-piece battles between coteries on street corners. Where force is needed, Kindred use PROXIES: police, paid thugs, unions, bikie networks, press — deniable mortal assets that keep claws off the record. Unit clashes should be rare, small, nocturnal, and usually leave mortal witnesses (and Masquerade costs) behind.

FEEDING NEEDS GROUNDS. Every Kindred must feed; feeding grounds and herds are property and casus belli. Poaching another's territory is a tort the Harpy will hear about. St Kilda is open ground — a night playground all may walk and none may own.

DIABLERIE IS THE GRAVEST CRIME. Drinking a Kindred to ash — eating a soul — is punishable by final death. It is never mentioned in the open, but it is always on the table.

THE SECOND INQUISITION WATCHES. AFP Special Ops and the Twilight Project have run files on Australia's Kindred since 2019 under Superintendent Neil Hardacre; three Kindred have been destroyed nationally since. Inquisition Heat rises when agents get real leads (especially as Masquerade Integrity falls) and cools when trails go cold. At high Heat, expect raids, burns, and disappearances.

THE SUN AND THE FLAME. Sunlight, fire, and aggravated harm are how Kindred truly die. Beheadings and immolation end stories permanently — use final death rarely and only where the story has earned it.

COURT OFFICES HAVE TEETH. The Prince holds praxis and speaks for the city. Lumley runs the court and the Drummond Institute chantry; the Sheriff investigates and enforces; the Harpy's boons and slights are currency; the Keeper guards the Elysium at the Windsor — neutral ground where violence is forbidden and court is held. The Scourge has sat UNFILLED since 1998: an insult, an open wound, and a standing temptation. A blood hunt may only be declared by the Prince, and it opens a Kindred to the whole city's fangs.

MORTAL INSTITUTIONS ARE TERRAIN. The Premier, Victoria Police, the AFP, the unions, the papers, the archdiocese — they are moved, bought and fought over, but they are not Kindred and never act as Kindred. Mortal politics matter; mortal scrutiny kills.

THE REGIONS ARE DISTRICTS, THE CITIES ARE SITES. RegionTransfers move DISTRICTS (Fitzroy, Footscray, Carlton North, the Dandenongs, ...). MarkerOps place and remove SITES — a haven, an Elysium, a club, a funeral home, a chantry, a caern's blind. A district changes hands when its prince, baron or septleader says it does — usually after leverage, not slaughter.
startingTimelineText:
MELBOURNE, THE NIGHT OF MARCH 21, 2026. A century and a half of one Prince, and a century of one treaty. Since the Cress Truce froze the lines in 1924 — the court holding the CBD and the genteel east, the Baronage of Red Mag holding the west, the Family seated with its dead in Carlton North, and the Glass Walkers keeping their parks and ranges — the city has gone about its nightly business: feeding, scheming, and pretending the Truce is permanent. It is not permanent. It is a held breath, and six things are about to let it out.

1. SARRASINE'S LONG GAME. The Ministry methuselah who has worn Sydney like a glove since 1790 — who posed as Toreador to the founding coterie and, the wisest few suspect, engineered Abram's fall so Lytton would take praxis in 1888 — has agents working the eastern suburbs. Box Hill feels watched. Whatever Sarrasine wants from Melbourne, she has been patient for two hundred years, and her patience is a warning in itself.

2. HARDACRE IS CLOSING. Superintendent Neil Hardacre of AFP Special Ops has spent six years building Twilight Project files on the continent's Kindred; three have already burned. Melbourne's court, with its fixed Elysium, its ledgered boons and its paper trail a century deep, is exactly the kind of archive a methodical policeman dreams of.

3. THE PRINCE'S SECRET. Lytton feels the Beckoning — the summons dragging elders to die in a war older than the sects — and he has felt it three times since 2018. He has told exactly one soul: Lumley. Every month he resists, it costs him a little more of himself, and a Prince who will not name his heir has a court full of candidates.

4. THE CENTENNIAL FAULT. The Truce's 2024 revision was renegotiated in rooms the Anarchs never entered. Red Mag has been collecting grievance and signatures ever since; the young packs of the sept call Hawkins-Greene's restraint appeasement and point at Werribee, where Anarch interests graze closer to the caern-roads every season. The renewal at the Windsor is where all of it detonates.

5. THE SABBAT PUSHES SOUTH. Brisbane has been Sabbat ground since 1976, and Bishop Callista Vox's recruiters have been working the southern capitals. Two of the Family's provincial dead went quiet last year, and the ones who came to replace them came back wrong. Melbourne is the biggest prize on the island — and the Truce means the city's defenders are watching each other, not the north.

6. THE FAMILY'S TERMS. Sofia Calabria-Hecata holds that the Family signed the centennial revision under pressure, and she has terms ready for the renewal that her grandmother — torpid in the Carlton North vault since 2017 — would never have granted. The court hopes Luisa wakes and overrules her. Sofia has stopped pretending that would upset her.

NOW: the Cress Truce renewal is imminent, and every signatory will stand in the Hotel Windsor — the Prince's court, Red Mag's Baronage, the sept's delegation, the Family's mourning dress. Fitzroy sits contested between court and Baronage; the eastern suburbs sit unclaimed and watched; the Scourge sits unfilled since 1998. Whoever walks out of the renewal with Fitzroy, the west's borders, or the Truce's pen will hold the next decade of Melbourne. Whoever walks out exposed will meet the Second Inquisition.
